newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Leftists call off plans to march to APEC venue.
newsitem.headline: Leftists call off plans to march to APEC venue.

text.p: The leaders of thousands of anti-APEC leftist protesters on Monday called off their motor cavalcade and march to the APEC summit venue at the Subic Bay freeport because it would be suicidal.

Police general Edgardo Aglipay, commander of riot troops who had set up blockades to prevent the protesters from reaching the freeport in Olongapo city, earlier said his men were ready to die to stop the march.
Aglipay said he could not allow the protesters to reach Olongapo because pro-APEC groups were gathering in the city and he did not want violence to erupt between the two groups.

Most of the estimated 7,000 protesters were in distinctive "jeepneys" -- colourful minibuses modelled on World War Two jeeps -- flying streamers with slogans decrying the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

"Considering the large number of our enemy, we will not sacrifice our bodies, we will not sacrifice our force because that will be suicide," leftist leader Nathaniel Santiago told the marchers assembled at Dinalupihan town, about 20 km (12 miles) from Olongapo.

Chief rally organiser Satur Ocampo said it was difficult to penetrate the police blockade blocking the final stretch to the former U.S. naval base at Subic Bay where the leaders of the 18 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation were holding their fourth annual summit.
"We are realistic enough to recognise that we cannot break through this last barricade," Ocampo told reporters, referring to the columns of riot police blocking the path of the marchers.
Police also put a crane, empty passenger buses and dump trucks across the road leading to Olongapo.

The leftist protesters stayed overnight at Dinalupihan, the town next to Subic, after travelling all the way from Manila. Their leaders said earlier they would press on towards Subic Bay at all costs.
